# BriefingCard

A card of what the person needs to know before they act on one thing. That thing may be a meeting, a customer or a handover; the card holds a status badge and the title, a quiet line, labelled rows of counts, links and small buttons, an agent's note, and a row of actions. The card is a region named by its title, the title is a heading, and the rows are a description list, so screen readers hear each label with its content. Rows with nothing in them are left out.

```tsx
import { BriefingCard } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/briefing-card/briefing-card";
```

## Example

```tsx
<BriefingCard
  title="Weekly sync"
  detail="In 25 min · 6 people"
  status="Needs you"
  statusTone="warning"
  items={[{ id: "chat", label: "Chat", content: "2 new · 1 asks you" }]}
  note={<AgentNote text={note.text} author="agent" name="Ouro" />}
  actions={<Button size="sm">Open chat</Button>}
/>
```

## Use instead when

- Use `Card` instead for content of your own shape, `DescriptionList` for a plain list of details, and `MeetingRow` for the meeting itself in an agenda.

## Props

Type: `BriefingCardProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | One row of actions at the end ("Open chat"). |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement (`mt-2`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `detail` | `ReactNode` |  | One quiet line under the title ("In 25 min · 6 people"). |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `3` | The heading level of the title, for the page's outline. |
| `items` (required) | `readonly BriefingCardItem[]` |  | The briefing's labelled rows, shown as a description list. |
| `note` | `ReactNode` |  | An agent's note about it, under the rows: an `AgentNote`, or a hint on how to get one. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `status` | `string` |  | Where things stand, as a short label in a badge before the title ("Needs you", "Up to date"). |
| `statusTone` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "destructive" \| "success" \| "warning"` | `"secondary"` | The status badge's color role from the theme, named after its token. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | What the briefing is about, its heading and its name for screen readers ("Weekly sync"). |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `heading`: Not a prop. The title is `title`: `<BriefingCard title="Weekly sync">`.
- `sections`: Not a prop. The rows are `items`: `<BriefingCard items={rows}>`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: BriefingCard merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with its own replaces it.[^layout-classes]

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `BriefingCardItem`

One labelled row of a `BriefingCard`.

```ts
interface BriefingCardItem {
  /** Identifies the row. */
  id: string;
  /** A short word in the margin ("Chat", "Last time", "Waiting on you"). */
  label: string;
  /** What to show: a count and a line, links, small buttons. A row with nothing in it is left out. */
  content: ReactNode;
}
```
